newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia reform working - U.S. investment official.
newsitem.headline: Russia reform working - U.S. investment official.

text.p: Russian economic reform appears to be moving ahead independently of political ups and downs, a U.S. investment official said on Friday, adding that investors were not put off by President Boris Yeltsin's poor health.

"The pace of economic progress in this country is almost operating independent of political events," Ruth Harkin, President of the U.S. Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC), told a news conference.
She said she believed economic changes were irreversible.
OPIC mainly provides political risk insurance to U.S. companies abroad and Harkin was in Moscow to discuss OPIC activity with Russian officials.
Harkin said the largest risks faced by investors were related to Russia's short track record with a market economy rather than political upheaval.
"I don't think any American investors are making investment decisions based on President Yeltsin's health," she said.
Yeltsin is in hospital with pneumonia and had heart surgery in November of last year.

Harkin predicted U.S. investors would increase investment in Russia in 1997, but said that legislative improvements such as amendments to an oil production-sharing law would sharply increase investment flows.
